title: a month of not-eating that's really a month of paying attention
hook: a month of not-eating that's really a month of paying attention

segments.voice: Yesterday: dhikr, remembrance on the fingers, and the quiet watching beside it. Your line was remember, again. What was your cue, and how often did it bring you back? Day eighteen.

Look back at the last few days. Water before the prayer. The prayer itself, the body bowing. The call. The Friday gathering. Remembrance on the fingers, and the quiet watching beside it. Every one of them is a way of paying attention, a few minutes at a time. Now stretch that to a whole month. Picture a kitchen at four in the morning, lights on, a family half asleep, eating dates and eggs and drinking as much water as they can before the sky starts to pale. Then nothing, no food, not even a sip of water, until sunset. For a whole month. Today: the month that takes all of that and makes it last.
screen: `A WEEK OF PAYING ATTENTION.` → `A KITCHEN AT FOUR IN THE MORNING.` → `THEN NOTHING UNTIL SUNSET.`

segments.voice: Ramadan is a month of the Islamic calendar, which follows the moon. Arabic dictionaries tie the name to a root, r-m-d, for scorching heat. Because the calendar is lunar, the month slides earlier every year, so over a lifetime it passes through every season, the long summer days and the short winter ones. The fast, sawm, is the fourth pillar. From the first light of dawn to sunset: no food, no drink. The Qur'an explains it in one line, in Pickthall's words: “Fasting is prescribed for you, even as it was prescribed for those before you, that ye may ward off (evil).” Notice what it says the fast is for. Not weight, not endurance. Taqwa, that careful awareness that wards off harm. The hunger is a tool, not the point. A hadith in Bukhari makes that sharp: whoever doesn't give up lying and acting on lies, God has no need of their giving up food and drink. An empty stomach with a sharp tongue has missed it. And the fast isn't meant to hurt anyone. The same passage excuses the sick and travelers, and scholars add the elderly, children, and women who are pregnant or nursing. Why this month? The Qur'an names Ramadan as the month in which the Qur'an was revealed. Muslims look for the Night of Power in its last ten nights, and the Qur'an says: “The Night of Power is better than a thousand months.” So at sunset, when the fast breaks, often with a date and water as the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ did, the hunger is real. So is the attention that comes with the first sip.
screen: `RAMADAN — FROM A ROOT FOR HEAT.` · `DAWN TO SUNSET: THE FOURTH PILLAR.` · `THAT YE MAY WARD OFF EVIL.` · `THE NIGHT OF POWER.` · then, large: `THE HUNGER IS A TOOL.`

segments.voice: The bell will give you about seventy-five seconds. Notice your body right now. Is there any hunger or thirst in it, even a little? Don't fix it. Just find where it lives: the stomach, the throat, the mouth. Then think of the next thing you'll eat or drink. Picture it, and picture receiving it slowly, like the first sip at sunset. If you pray, you can hold the word alhamdulillah ready for that moment. The bell holds the time.
Ramadan. The month of fasting, dawn to sunset, and the month of the Qur'an's revelation. Eighteenth word.
Your line: hunger teaches. Today, eat one meal or drink one glass of water without your phone, and notice the first bite or the first sip. Day eighteen.

screen: `DAY 18 COUNTS.` → `TOMORROW: THE PILLAR THAT'S ABOUT MONEY.`

howItsDone: During Ramadan, adult Muslims who are able fast from dawn to sunset, eat a pre-dawn meal called suhur, break the fast at sunset with iftar, often with dates and water, and mosques hold extra night prayers.

fork.setup: it's Ramadan. you've fasted all day, and at four in the afternoon a coworker says something that makes you furious. what does the hadith say about your fast?

fork.reveal: the hunger is a tool, not the point. God has no need of the fast of someone who won't give up lying (Bukhari).

original.note: Arabic: the month of the fast, from r-m-d, a root for scorching heat.

trapdoor: what you thought: a month when Muslims don't eat.
what it means: Ramadan — a month of fasting dawn to sunset, aimed at taqwa, careful awareness, not hunger for its own sake.
what a scholar hears: r-m-d, scorching heat; a lunar month drifting through the seasons; 2:183 ties the fast to those before; and 2:185 names it the month the Qur'an was revealed.

sources.ref: Sunan Abi Dawud 2356; Jami' at-Tirmidhi 696 (breaking the fast with dates and water)

notes: Pickthall 2:183 and 97:3 quoted from memory; confirm exact wording ('O ye who believe! Fasting is prescribed for you, even as it was prescribed for those before you, that ye may ward off (evil);').
Pickthall spells the month 'Ramadhan' (2:185); the script uses Ramadan and doesn't quote 2:185.
Root r-m-d (ramad, intense heat): a common explanation of the name; confirm.
Fasting also excludes marital relations; the script mentions food and drink only, for a general audience. Confirm acceptable.
Exemptions: 2:184–185 name the sick and travelers (and those for whom it is very hard); children, the elderly, pregnant and nursing women from jurists and hadith. Confirm.
Hadith numbers (Bukhari 1903; Abu Dawud 2356, Tirmidhi 696) cited from memory; confirm.
Look back is in the hook: the practices of days 13–17 (wudu, salat, adhan, Jumu'ah, dhikr), updated after the move from day 14 to day 18.

The Night of Power's place in the last ten nights comes from hadith, and its exact night is debated (many seek it on the odd nights, often the 27th). The script now says Muslims look for it there rather than stating it as settled.

Editor review 2026-10-01: review screen showed 'MURAQABA — WATCH YOUR OWN BREATH' though yesterday's word was dhikr; fixed. Cut uncited numbers (ninth month, 29 or 30 days, about eleven days a year) and 'first revealed' (2:185 says only that the Qur'an was revealed in the month); the narrator no longer says what the month has taught people. Keeper: the lunar drift and month number are standard facts and could be restored with a source.
